If your LCL shipment from China is due in New York/New Jersey just before Christmas, keep the pickup date provisional until the destination freight station confirms that your individual shipment is available and released, and your trucker can collect it within the station’s holiday hours. The vessel may arrive while the container is still waiting to move to the warehouse or be unpacked. Ask for three things on the same email thread: confirmed availability for your house bill of lading, the warehouse’s last free day and cutoff time, and the first pickup slot or permitted collection window. If those dates don’t line up, get a storage estimate before dispatching a truck.

  • Track the vessel for arrival and your house bill for pickup.
  • Get the last free day and holiday counting rule from the destination freight station or its agent.
  • Give your trucker a confirmed collection window and book the receiving warehouse separately.

Track five dates from port arrival to truck pickup

Ask the destination agent for the name and address of the container freight station (CFS), the warehouse where the shared container is unpacked and individual shipments are made available. If the routing shows New York/New Jersey as the port of discharge and an inland CFS as the place of delivery, use the inland station’s pickup details. Keep the house bill of lading (HBL) handy when asking about your own freight. A container number helps track the shared box, while the house bill identifies the shipment you want to collect.

MilestoneWhat to ask forWho confirms it
Vessel arrivalLatest ETA or actual arrival, named marine terminal, and discharge status. Ask when the container is expected to move to the CFS.Ocean carrier or destination forwarder
Container unpackingHas the shared container reached the CFS? Is unpacking scheduled or complete? Have the pieces under my HBL been checked in?CFS or destination agent
Cargo availability noticeIs my HBL available for pickup? Ask for the written notice or live portal status, any outstanding customs or freight release, and pickup references.CFS or destination agent, with the broker confirming customs status
Last free dayWhat is the exact date and local cutoff time? What starts free time, do weekends and holidays count, and what charges apply if pickup slips?CFS or destination agent applying the warehouse terms
Truck pickup appointmentIs a reservation needed? Get a confirmed slot or collection window, the correct pickup address, required driver paperwork, and a separate delivery appointment if the receiver requires one.CFS, trucker and receiving warehouse

Check the terminal and the freight station separately

APM Terminals Port Elizabeth marks Friday, December 25, 2026, and Friday, January 1, 2027, as no-work ILA holidays on its published calendar. For dates such as December 24 and December 31, check the terminal’s specific notice for gate hours. Then ask the named CFS for its own holiday schedule, including the last time a driver can check in. A terminal notice covers the terminal. Your collection window comes from the facility releasing the individual freight.

Suppose your ship is due December 23 and you need the pallets at your warehouse on December 24. Ask the destination agent whether the container transfer and unpack are expected before your trucker’s latest workable pickup. If the agent only has a forecast, keep the truck on a tentative booking where possible and agree a fallback window with the receiver. Once the freight is checked in and released, compare the available pickup slot with both the CFS gate cutoff and the receiving appointment.

Get the last free day in writing

Start with the free time for your cartons or pallets at the CFS. The ocean carrier’s terminal demurrage clock concerns the container at the marine terminal. Ask which charge you are looking at, which party bills it, and which reference the charge applies to.

For the CFS, ask for the exact start event, the last free calendar date and local cutoff, and whether closed days count under the applicable terms. If the earliest available truck slot falls after the last free day, send the conflicting dates to the destination agent. Ask whether another permitted collection window is open, whether the station will confirm an extension, and what storage will cost if you collect later. Get any agreed revision in writing before budgeting on it.

Give the trucker a pickup that can actually happen

Send the actual CFS address, HBL, pickup or release reference, piece count, packed dimensions and weight, and gate cutoff. Ask the dispatcher to confirm the driver has the documents required by that station. If the destination agent is arranging door delivery, ask who owns the CFS pickup and who will update you when the delivery appointment moves.

For the delivery leg, tell the trucker what the receiver can handle and where the freight should be handed over. Use the warehouse unloading checklist to confirm the dock, liftgate or inside delivery before booking that leg.

Send DDNZ your shipment details on WhatsApp. Include the China origin, U.S. delivery ZIP code, packed dimensions and weights, cargo-ready date, and the date your warehouse needs the freight. If the shipment is already booked, add the HBL and latest destination notice so we can help identify which pickup details still need confirmation.

Common questions

Can I collect LCL freight on the vessel arrival date?

Plan pickup from the destination CFS once it verifies that your HBL is available for collection, the applicable releases are in place, and a truck can collect within the station’s hours. Use the vessel arrival date to start those checks.

Does an arrival notice confirm that my cargo is available?

Check the arrival notice for shipment details and next steps. For dispatch, use the destination agent’s confirmed pickup status for your HBL and check for any remaining freight or customs hold.

Do Christmas and New Year’s Day count toward CFS storage?

Ask the named station or destination agent how it counts holidays under the terms for your shipment. Request the exact last free day and local cutoff in writing before committing to a truck.
